messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty alert — GPU pool `east1-primary` has sustained queue growth and autoscaler errors. Observed 5m avg queue > 2000 requests; requests hitting throttles. Customer impact: increased 429s and streaming stalls for a subset of hosted customers in us-east. Paging @ryan_oncall :rotating_light:

ryan_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Toggling to incident channel. grabbing logs and checking autoscaler state.

autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler event: attempted_scale_up -> desired=120, launched=0, error="quotaExceeded: reached max_instances=100"; last_error_ts=2143500023

ryan_oncall: copy. looks like we hit provider quota + our max_instances cap. can someone confirm whether this is cloud-quotas or our config limit? @lucas_infra @priya_traffic

lucas_infra: digging into cloud console now. quick note: there were a few recent large canaries in east1 earlier today, might've used up ephemeral quota. opening ticket with provider support but not expecting immediate quota bump.

priya_traffic: if we can't scale east1, we should spill traffic to backups. I'll start a controlled spillover to eu1 and lower per-tenant concurrency to reduce pressure. expect higher latencies for affected requests.

ryan_oncall: good plan. run it and post commands you run so SRE can audit. also let's raise incident severity to Sev2 and notify CS/PM.

priya_traffic: running routing update now:

```bash
# route 40% of traffic from east1-primary to eu1 as immediate spillover
redwoodctl routing update --from east1-primary --to eu1 --weight 0.4 --immediate
redwoodctl routing show --source east1-primary
```

priya_traffic: routing call successful. new policy:
- east1-primary: 60%
- eu1: 40%
Note: streaming sessions will see reconnects; we issued a short-lived session-sticky fallback.

deploy-bot: Canary deploys detected earlier today to east1: +12 instances at 10:12 UTC, +8 instances at 11:05 UTC. No failures reported at deploy time.

lucas_infra: cloud support responded — quota increase request created but ETA 4-8 hours. Manual immediate mitigations: starting shared warm pool `shared-buffer-1` in us-central and moving some stateless replica traffic there. Command: 

```bash
# provision standby pool on GCP (short-hand)
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize shared-buffer-1 --size=20 --zone=us-central1-a
# attach model-serving image and warm cache
```

ryan_oncall: nice. @maya_support can you pull customer impact metrics and surface top affected tenants? we need to prioritize outreach.

maya_support: support dashboard shows ~120 related tickets in last 30m. Top 5 tenants by error volume: AcmeCorp (30% 429s), ShopLarge (27%), NoteApp (22%), EduStream (18%), QuickForms (15%). Opening a dedicated thread with templates for status updates.

emma_pm: prepping customer comms. we'll highlight mitigation & ETA. please add affected SLAs. Also adding sales to notify enterprise accounts.

priya_traffic: additionally applied temporary per-tenant concurrency cap to reduce noise from noisy tenants: `per_route_concurrency=50` for non-enterprise routes. This should reduce queue pressure.

autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler diagnostics: scale_attempts=5, last_error="max_instances_reached". Observed provisioning failures: 2 transient API timeouts + 3 quota rejections.

ryan_oncall: timeline so far: 2143500000 alert triggered -> 2143500023 autoscaler quota error -> 2143500075 routing change applied (40% eu1) -> 2143500200 warm pool provisioned -> 2143500300 per-tenant caps applied. Queue length trending down but still above target.

lucas_infra: confirming: we've drained ~35% of backlog via routing + buffer pool. remaining drain is slow because streaming requests hold KV cache; recommend a selective eviction of long-tail KV to free memory for active sessions. will execute in 5m.

priya_traffic: side-effect: eu1 latency +50-120ms for these requests. monitoring metrics and adjusting weight if error rate climbs in eu1.

maya_support: putting together initial customer bulletin. draft: "We experienced elevated throttling in us-east due to capacity provisioning limits. Traffic has been partially rerouted to eu1 and temporary per-tenant caps applied. We continue to stabilize and will share a follow-up postmortem."

ryan_oncall: action items (owners):
- incident lead: ryan_oncall (coordinate, triage)
- routing & mitigations: priya_traffic (spillover, weights)
- infra/quota & buffer pool: lucas_infra (provider ticket + warm pools)
- customer comms: emma_pm + maya_support
- postmortem: ryan_oncall + lucas_infra

emma_pm: marking incident Sev2 in tracker (INC-2143500000). scheduling 1hr bridge for post-incident review in 3h.

ryan_oncall: temporary measures in place. primary follow-ups for postmortem: increase max_instances limit, add global standby buffer pool pre-warmed across regions, implement autoscaler guardrail to prefer spillover earlier (reduce aggressive local scale when quota near limit), and add alerting for cloud quota exhaustion.

priya_traffic: one more: we should surface a quick CLI snippet for SRE runbook to reroute in emergencies:

```bash
# emergency spillover to fallback region (idempotent)
redwoodctl routing emergency-spill --from east1-primary --to eu1 --percent 50 --reason "autoscaler_quota"
```

ryan_oncall: thanks everyone. continuing to monitor. if error rates spike again we'll increase spillover and throttle non-critical routes. reopening this thread for timeline updates and final notes for postmortem.

deploy-bot: Notifying infra-deploys channel: no deploy rollbacks triggered.

ryan_oncall: closing active paging window for now — handoff to lucas_infra for quota follow-up and priya_traffic for routing adjustments. will reconvene for postmortem. :thumbsup:
